Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
1215 PM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

*  No significant changes from earlier forecasts. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 108 AM Tuesday...

1) Hot 90+ degree temperatures return Thursday and Friday. A slow 
moving cold front will bring a good shot at showers and 
thunderstorms and much needed rain/cooler temperatures, especially 
over the weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 108 AM Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Hot temperatures return mid through late week. A 
slow moving cold front will bring a good shot at showers and 
thunderstorms and much needed rain/cooler temperatures, especially 
over the weekend. 

It appears widespread 90+ degree temperatures will return Thursday 
and Friday as surface high pressure will be offshore and the 
mid/upper level ridging will shift to the SE states. It appears the 
hottest day will likely be Thursday under the ridge. A break in the 
ridge and a developing Ohio Valley to central Appalachians trough 
will approach Friday lowering mid level heights enough so that the 
temperatures may back off a few degrees. Expect lower to mid 90s 
on Thursday and upper 80s to lower 90s Friday. These temperatures 
will back off considerably this weekend as the upper trough develops 
over the Ohio into the TN valley region increasing moisture, 
cloudiness. and likely showers/storms over the weekend. Expect highs 
in the 80s except around 90 in the SE.

The aforementioned approaching trough will also be accompanied by a 
pre-frontal trough and a surface front (or two). These features 
should allow for a likelihood 60-70 percent chance of mainly PM 
showers/storms both Saturday and Sunday. We will update any severe 
threat in upcoming forecasts. At the moment, it appears wind shear 
may be lacking but instability will be high. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
As of 1215 PM Tuesday...

VFR conditions are likely to dominate across central NC for the next 
24 hours, with high confidence. High pressure centered near the Mid 
Atlantic coast will continue to extend SW across our area through 
Wed, as its center pushes slowly E and further offshore. This will 
keep cloud cover minimal, restricted to some flat cu and sct mid and 
high clouds at most. Due to good radiational cooling conditions 
including fair skies and nearly calm air tonight, patchy shallow fog 
producing brief MVFR vsbys is possible at RWI toward and around 
daybreak. Elsewhere, the fog risk is low. Surface winds will remain 
light and variable or from the E or NE. 

Looking beyond 18z Wed, VFR conditions should prevail across central 
NC through at least Thu, with generally dry weather, although an 
isolated storm is possible in our far SE late Thu. Then, late Thu 
night into Fri morning, there is a risk for fog and low clouds 
producing sub-VFR conditions, mainly in our SE (FAY). The chance for 
showers and storms and resulting flight restrictions increases late 
Fri and reaches a peak Sat into Sun, as a cold front moves in from 
the NW and stalls across the Carolinas. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Badgett 
AVIATION...Hartfield

FXUS62 KILM 081710
AFDILM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
110 PM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No major changes were made, only some adjustments to the key 
messages. The aviation section was updated for the 18Z TAFs. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Drier weather initially, then warmer with rain chances 
returning during the week.

2) Surf hazards will continue through the remainder of today.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Drier weather initially, then warmer with rain 
chances returning during the week.

Ridging aloft, currently from the Central Plains into the MS 
Valley, will build across the Southeast U.S. during Wednesday. 
This pattern will keep the column mostly dry along with surface 
high pressure that will be far off the NC coast at this time. 
The H5 ridge will shift off the coast during Thursday with weak 
return flow allowing the higher PWAT environment to the south to
spread northward again. During Thursday will maintain the 
highest PoPs across the SC zones (40-60%) with some across the 
NC zones (20-40%). The high PWATs will continue across the 
forecast area through the weekend with a front potentially 
stalling/weakening across the area this weekend. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Surf hazards will continue through the 
remainder of today.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION...Ely winds will continue to result 
in rip currents, mainly for the E facing beaches, and a moderate
to strong longshore current for the S facing beaches. May see 
some of these conditions linger into Wednesday, but the fetch 
that resulted in these conditions today is projected to be 
weaker Wednesday. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions will prevail with a dry column in place and the 
low- level trajectory helping to steer any shower activity well 
south of the terminals. SCT cumulus will dissipate this evening.
Ely winds are expected at all terminals through today with some
gusts, with light winds on tap tonight. 

Extended Outlook...Predominantly VFR conditions continue with 
dry high pressure in place, with restrictions possibly returning
in convection at times Thursday through the weekend.

&&

.MARINE...
Tonight through Sunday: High pressure off the VA/NC coast will 
focus the stronger ENE fetch just south of the South Santee 
marine zone with the weaker winds generally north of Cape Fear. 
The surface ridge axis will extend nearly E-W into NC tonight 
into Wednesday morning allowing for lighter Ely winds. The high 
will shift farther offshore during Wednesday into Thursday 
allowing for additional veering with the gradient light enough 
for winds around 10 kts. An inland trough will become 
established by Friday and with high pressure much farther 
offshore S-SWly winds will return. More uncertainty exists this 
weekend with a front possibly stalling/weakening across the 
waters. Seas will be greatest through the remainder of today and
tonight especially across the southern ILM waters, then 3 ft or
less through much of the upcoming period.

&&

.ILM WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...High Risk for Rip Currents until 8 PM EDT this evening for NCZ106-
     108.
     Coastal Flood Advisory from 7 PM to 10 PM EDT this evening for 
     NCZ107.
     Beach Hazards Statement until 8 PM EDT this evening for NCZ110.
SC...High Risk for Rip Currents until 8 PM EDT this evening for SCZ056.
     Beach Hazards Statement until 8 PM EDT this evening for SCZ054.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
1122 AM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- High Risk for Rip Currents Today Most Local Beaches. High Risk Wednesday
All Local Beaches. Elevated Rip Current Risk through Thursday

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms Tuesday to Sunday. Main
Hazards: Locally Heavy Rain, Lightning & Gusty Winds to 40 mph

&&

.UPDATE...

Showers have yet to become more organized across the coastal waters 
with only widely isolated showers having moved onshore this morning 
from the JAX beaches and into portions of Jacksonville. The 12Z JAX 
sounding shows much more dry air in the mid levels compared to 
yesterday with Precipitable Water levels below 2.0 inches (1.97 
inches) which is the 75th percentile compared to climatology for 
early September. Some drier air is also noted just above the 
boundary layer above very moist low levels. The drier air is more 
expansive aloft across SE GA where Precipitable Water levels range 
1.4 inches inland to 1.7 inches along the SE GA coast.  

The high to the north will shift to the NC/VA coast this afternoon 
to early evening as the coastal trough remains over the offshore 
waters to the east. Showers will gradually increase in coverage over 
the coastal waters through noon as moist low level onshore flow and 
lift due to the trough and coastal convergence combine and produce 
some thin bands of showers that will shift onshore the SE GA and NE 
FL coast inland WSW to I-75 with scattered coverage becoming more 
numerous along the SE GA coast. Strong heating will allow more than 
2,000 J/kg of CAPE today, especially away from the coast towards I-
75 where the ENE winds will interact with a pinned Gulf seabreeze 
along the nature coast and a lingering front near to just south of 
north central FL, producing scattered thunderstorms coverage from 
Gainesville to St Augustine southward into Marion county. 

Breezy winds 10-15 mph with gusts to 25 mph expected along the coast 
into the St Johns river while further inland decreasing to 8-12 mph 
with gusts to 20 mph. A mix of sun and clouds from the occasional 
onshore moving coastal showers will limit highs to the mid 80s along 
the coast, upper 80s along I-95, and the low 90s inland near I-75 
and inland SE GA.

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...
Highlights Through Tonight:

- Breezy onshore/easterly winds today

- Passing gusty showers & inland mainly afternoon storms

- High Risk for Rip Currents Southeast GA Beaches & Elevated Tides

Taste of fall continues for southeast GA and northeast Florida today 
with waves of coastal showers and increasingly breezy northeast to 
east winds as a weak coastal trough develops over the adjacent 
coastal waters. Low chance (< 10%) of a morning coastal thunderstorm 
focused south of St. Augustine where deeper moisture resides near 
the departing surface front across north-central FL. Through the 
day, shower activity will expand inland with diurnal heating, but 
convective depth will be limited across much of southeast GA and and 
near and north of the FL Interstate 10 corridor as drier mid and 
upper level air from the north filters across the area. Thus, 
expected mostly diurnally driven showers into the afternoon for 
locations north of I-10 while the better coverage of afternoon 
showers and thunderstorms focuses across north-central FL, generally 
from St. Augustine toward Gainesville southward. 

This evening, inland showers fade while coastal showers and isolated 
thunderstorms continue as the coastal trough lingers offshore. After 
midnight, the coastal trough begins to break down and weaken as 
surface high pressure offshore of the mid-Atlantic region settles 
southward. Could see an influx of shower activity toward daybreak, 
shifting farther inland as the trough axis also shifts westward. 

High temperatures trend a little warmer into today nearing 90 toward 
the Interstate 75 corridor while breezy onshore winds keeps coastal 
areas cooler with highs in the mid 80s. Tonight, lows will continue 
to range in the 70s to near 80 toward the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TUESDAY THROUGH 12Z WEDNESDAY/...
VFR ceilings and occasional MVFR ceilings expected through 14-16Z 
as moist flow between a coastal trough to the east and high pressure 
to the north brings in periodic showers onshore and inland.
 
Northeast winds around 10 knots at the coast will increase to 12-15 
knots with gusts to 25 knots while lighter inland winds 4-6 knots 
increase by 16Z to 10-12 knots with gusts near 20 knots. Have VCSH 
for all sites this afternoon with some MVFR ceilings as times as the 
coastal showers move onshore as the trough remains east of the 
terminals, but am including PROB30 groups for TSRA at VQQ, GNV, SGJ 
while PROB30 groups in place for JAX and CRG for MVFR VSBY and CIGs, 
while SSI will remain north of the better batch of showers this 
afternoon with no PROB30 groups as dry air limits coverage there. 

VFR conditions prevail after 00Z-02Z and shower chances inland will 
diminish after 00Z while persisting at SSI through 06Z as the 
coastal trough weakens and moves onshore the Georgia coast as high 
pressure to the north shifts more to the northeast. Then, MVFR 
ceilings will redevelop in the early morning hours at GNV, JAX, and 
VQQ after 06Z.

&&

.MARINE...


A coastal trough develops today and persists through Wednesday 
morning with waves of gusty showers and isolated thunderstorms. The 
trough begins to weaken Wednesday night into Thursday as high 
pressure builds northeast of the region. The high will then extend 
across the Florida peninsula Friday into the weekend with a return 
of southwest winds and the afternoon east coast sea breeze.

Onshore ENE winds strengthen today with building surf. With elevated 
ENE wind surge over the waters, extended the high rip current risk 
southward from southeast GA to included northeast FL beaches down 
the St. Johns county coast. Flagler county remains under a Moderate 
rip current risk today. Surf heights increase to 2-4 ft through the 
evening. High rip current risk likely for all local beaches 
Wednesday due to persistent onshore flow and elevated surf.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

A cold front will be sit across central Florida through midweek 
before weakening and dissipating by Thursday evening. Increased rain 
and storm chances are forecast each day as onshore winds brings 
morning coastal showers which will spread towards inland locations 
throughout the day and increase in coverage. There remains potential 
for locally heavy downpours through mid-week. Overall, dispersion 
will be fair to good Tuesday and Wednesday. Winds will shift to 
southerly/southwesterly Thursday through the weekend as ridging 
develops off the east coast.

Fog Potential: Gusty and erratic winds will occur with thunderstorm 
activity. Patchy inland morning fog possible each day.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

Coastal water levels begin to increase this week with the approach 
of the New Moon on Sept 11th and breezy onshore easterly winds late 
Tonight through Wednesday, with the peak winds across the local 
waters and coast Tuesday. At this time, guidance and observations 
show that water levels will be near and just above the action stage 
through Wednesday both along the local Atlantic coast and within the 
St. Johns River basin.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  90  73  90  72 /  10  10  60  20 
SSI  87  79  87  78 /  60  60  60  30 
JAX  89  75  89  75 /  30  40  40  10

GNV  89  74  91  73 /  30  10  70  30 
OCF  90  74  91  74 /  50  10  70  30

     333.

MARINE...None.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
511 AM MDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Slightly cooler today with a chance of thunderstorms mainly over
  the Palmer Divide and southeast plains. A few strong storms 
  possible with gusty winds, hail and locally heavy rainfall.

- Mainly dry Wednesday through Friday with warmer temperatures for
  Thursday and Friday.

- Return to more unsettled pattern and cooler weather favored for
  next weekend with a chance of thunderstorms mainly on Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Monday/...
Issued at 239 AM MDT Tue Sep 8 2026

The flow aloft will become more WSW today as best monsoon 
moisture shifts mainly across srn portions of the area. Meanwhile,
a secondary surge of drier air in the lower levels will move 
across the plains. By aftn, MLCAPE will range between 500-800 j/kg
and be confined to the srn foothills, Palmer Divide and over sern
portions of the CWA. With decent shear in place, can't rule out a
few stronger storms in this area by late aftn thru the early 
evening hours. PW values will still be around 150 percent of 
normal, in the same general area, so may see locally heavy 
rainfall as well. Over the rest of the area, shower and tstms will
be more isolated in coverage. Highs today will drop back into the
mid to upper 80's across the plains.

For Wed, drier in westerly flow aloft will be over the area as a 
cold front move across.  As a result, expect dry conditions with 
cooler temps as highs finally drop back to more seasonal levels.
By Wed night, low level southeast flow will develop which will lead 
to some return of moisture across the plains.  Meanwhile, a weak 
disturbance embedded in WNW flow aloft may bring some nocturnal 
tstms to portions of the sern plains overnight.  Current data, keeps 
most of this activity over sern CO with srn Lincoln county being on 
the nrn fringe. For now, have kept in chc pops mainly across srn 
portions of Lincoln county.

On Thu, the flow aloft will remain WNW as southerly level flow is 
across the plains.  MLCAPE will rise up to 1000 j/kg over portions 
of the plains by aftn.  For now, chances for tstms look on the low 
side as I can't find a focus for activity, however, that doesn't 
mean there couldn't be an isold storm or two across the plains by 
late aftn. Meanwhile, temps will begin to warm as readings reach 
the upper 80's to lower 90's over nern CO.

Looking ahead to Fri, zonal flow aloft will be over the area as a 
sfc lee trough develops over the plains.  This will lead to another 
warm day as highs rise into the upper 80's to mid 90's over the 
plains.  Meanwhile, models have some mid level moisture embedded in 
the flow, which may lead to a slight chc of higher based 
showers/tstms over the higer terrain.  Across the plains, MLCAPE is 
rather minimal so chances of precip look low.

For Fri night into Sat, zonal flow aloft will continue.  Meanwhile, 
a cold front will move across Fri night into Sat morning.  This 
front will drop temps back to more seasonal levels across nern CO. 
Once again MLCAPE is rather minimal and confined to the higher 
terrain.  Thus will keep in a slight chc for showers/tstms 
mainly across the mtns.

By Sun, an upper level trough will move into the nrn Rockies with 
increasing WSW flow aloft across the area.  At the sfc, a lee trough 
will intensify east of the mtns with southerly low level flow across 
the plains.  MLCAPE is fcst to increase to around 1000 j/kg over the 
plains east of a pseudo dryline.  Thus may see a few stronger storms 
by late aftn thru the evening hours.  Highs on Sun, will likely rise 
back to above normal levels.

Looking ahead to Mon, rather dry WSW flow aloft will be over the 
areas a cool front affects the plains.  Latest data, doesn't show 
much low level moisture behind the front so it may end up dry with 
temps dropping back to seasonal normals.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Wednesday/...
Issued at 506 AM MDT Tue Sep 8 2026

Light and variable winds early this morning wil become NE by 16z
and then more easterly by 19z.  By 21z, expect a more ESE wind.
There is still a 20-30 percent chance of tstms in the 21z to 01z
time period. However, the best chc of storms will stay south of
BJC and DIA and will likely impact APA. Thus have kept prob30 at 
both BJC and DIA with a tempo at APA. By 01z the threat of storms
will end with winds becoming SE. By 04z winds will have a more 
southerly direction. Late tonight, a cold front will move across 
between 09z and 10z with winds shifting to the north.

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
